# 1 Analysis approach

Our project uses **supervised ML** to predict engagement of reddit posts on
subreddit `r/wallstreetbets`. We also extend the original dataset with some
existing sentiment analysis tool to detect the presence of sarcasm in post
titles and/or post bodies, which is explained in checkpoint 2 and is omitted in
the current analysis.

To create the dataset for ML, we allocate 80% of posts to training and 20% to testing,
stratified on `high_engagement` (whether the comment count exceeds the median.)
We use the same five stratified cross-validation folds within training for every model. 
Recipes estimate preprocessing parameters within each analysis fold,
and final workflows are refitted on the full training set. The random split 
evaluates held-out posts from the historical mixture for posts span across Jan 2021 to Mar 2025.
A random seed `42` is set for replicable analysis.

The baseline uses `log_body_words`, `no_body`, and `market_open`, with an additional version including linear title and body sarcasm terms. Expanded models add post type, NY posting hour, day of week, year, and title length, caps ratio, punctuation, ticker, emoji, and keyword flags. Expanded linear regression and lasso use a spline for title sarcasm. Linear-model recipes normalize numeric predictors and dummy-code factors; the random forest retains factors. `score` is excluded because it accrues after posting. Comparing the reduced baseline with expanded models measures the combined benefit of additional features and model flexibility; expanded linear regression provides a closer reference for lasso and random forest using the same predictor information.

All our models are trying to predict the log-transformed comment count for each
post (`log(1+comment_count)`), so the log transform
compresses the right tail, and the +1 keeps posts with zero comments.
We have the following models being tested and compared in our project:

- Base model: 
  - Model type: linear regression
  - Predictor:  
    - `log_body_words`: Log transformed word count for post body
    - `no_body`: Whether the post have post body at all (due to post being
    link-only, image only...)
    - `market_open`: Whether the post was posted at a time when NYSE was during
      regular opening hours 
- Advanced model 1 (linear, extended features):
  - Model type: Multiple linear regression, fitted through tidymodels with the
    `lm` engine. This model extends the baseline with more information about
    the title, post type, and posting time.
  - Predictor:
    - `log_body_words`: Log transformed word count for post body
    - `no_body`: Whether the post body is missing or empty
    - `log_title_chars`: Log transformed number of characters in the title
    - `title_caps_ratio`: Proportion of letters in the title that are uppercase
    - `title_has_question`: Whether the title contains a question mark
    - `title_has_exclaim`: Whether the title contains an exclamation mark
    - `title_has_ticker`: Whether the title contains a `$TICKER` cashtag
    - `title_has_emoji`: Whether the title contains an emoji or other symbol
    - `title_has_kw`: Whether the title contains keywords such as YOLO, DD,
      gain, gains, loss, or losses
    - `post_type`: Type of post inferred from its URL: text, image, video,
      gallery, or link
    - `ny_dow`: Day of the week when the post was created, in New York time
    - `ny_hour_f`: Posting hour in New York time, treated as a categorical variable
    - `post_year`: Year when the post was created
  - Sarcasm comparison: We test this model with and without `title_sarcasm`
    and `body_sarcasm`. In the version with sarcasm, `title_sarcasm` uses a
    [natural spline with four degrees of freedom](https://recipes.tidymodels.org/reference/step_ns.html)
    to allow a nonlinear relationship with log comment count, while
    `body_sarcasm` enters as a linear term.
  - Preprocessing: Numeric predictors are standardized, categorical predictors
    are dummy coded, and predictors with zero variance are removed.
    `market_open` is replaced by the more detailed `ny_hour_f` variable.
  - Hyperparameters: No hyperparameters are tuned; the spline degrees of
    freedom are fixed at four.
- Advanced model 2 (lasso, extended features):
  - Model type: Lasso regression
    fitted through tidymodels with the `glmnet` engine. This is a linear model
    with an L1 penalty that shrinks coefficients and can set some coefficients
    to zero, providing variable selection and helping control overfitting.
  - Predictor: The same expanded predictors as advanced model 1, including
    both `title_sarcasm` and `body_sarcasm`. Title sarcasm uses the same
    natural spline with four degrees of freedom, while body sarcasm enters
    as a linear term. The current lasso model includes sarcasm only.
  - Preprocessing: The same standardization, dummy coding, and removal of
    predictors with zero variance as advanced model 1.
  - Hyperparameters: `mixture = 1` specifies a pure lasso penalty. We tune
    `penalty` over 20 logarithmically spaced values from `10^-5` to `10^-1`,
    choosing the value with the lowest mean log-scale RMSE across the five
    training cross-validation folds.
- Advanced model 3 (random forest, extended features):
  - Model type: Random forest regression
    fitted through tidymodels with the `ranger` engine. This model averages
    predictions from 300 decision trees and can capture nonlinear relationships
    and interactions between predictors.
  - Predictor: The same expanded predictors as advanced model 1. The version
    with sarcasm adds the original `title_sarcasm` and `body_sarcasm` scores;
    no spline transformation is applied because the trees can model nonlinear
    relationships directly.
  - Sarcasm comparison: We test versions with and without the two sarcasm
    scores. The version without sarcasm uses the hyperparameters selected for
    the version with sarcasm, keeping these settings fixed for the comparison.
  - Preprocessing: Numeric predictors retain their original scales, and
    categorical predictors remain factors rather than being dummy coded.
  - Hyperparameters: The number of trees is fixed at 300. We tune `mtry`
    (number of candidate predictors considered at each split) from 3 to 12
    and `min_n` (minimum node size for splitting) from 10 to 100, using three
    values for each parameter to create nine combinations. We select the
    combination with the lowest mean log-scale RMSE across the same five
    training cross-validation folds.

The primary comparison uses RMSE on `log_comms`, with MAE and R-squared as supporting metrics, for every model. 
Secondary ROC AUC uses each model's predicted log count to rank the same high/low engagement outcome; 
it does not measure count accuracy. Cross-validation results for selected tuning parameters may be optimistic, 
so the held-out test results provide the final performance assessment. Package versions are recorded in `renv.lock`.

### Post-only data with sarcasm scores

Load the post-only data with sarcasm scores created in Checkpoint 2, and rebuild the derived variables.

```{r}
# load post-only data
data_wsb2022_sarcasm = read_csv("./data/wsb_2022_postonly_sarcasm.csv")

# peek
data_wsb2022_sarcasm |>
  head(5)
```

```{r}
# Derivate meaningful variables (same as Checkpoint 2)
data = data_wsb2022_sarcasm |>
  # created time in NY timezone (wallstreet)
  dplyr::mutate(
    created_ny_time = format(
      lubridate::with_tz(lubridate::as_datetime(created, tz = "UTC"), tzone = "America/New_York"),
      "%H:%M:%S"
    ),
    created_ny_hour_bin = {
      ny_hour = as.integer(substr(created_ny_time, 1L, 2L))
      hour_label = dplyr::if_else(
        is.na(ny_hour), NA_character_, paste0(ny_hour, "-", (ny_hour + 1L) %% 24L)
      )
      factor(hour_label, levels = paste0(0:23, "-", (1:24) %% 24), ordered = TRUE)
    },
    # posts without body
    no_body = is.na(body) | trimws(body) == "",
    # post content word count
    body_work_count = stringr::str_count(dplyr::coalesce(body, ""), "\\S+"),
    # posts with only a link
    link_only = {
      body_text = stringr::str_trim(dplyr::coalesce(body, ""))
      (stringr::str_detect(body_text, "(?i)^https?://\\S+$") |
        stringr::str_detect(body_text, "(?i)^\\[[^\\]]+\\]\\(https?://\\S+\\)$")) &
        !stringr::str_detect(
          body_text,
          "(?i)https?://(?:[a-z0-9-]+\\.)*(?:reddit\\.com|redd\\.it)(?=[:/?#]|$)"
        )
    }
  )
```

Apply the same cleaning and quality assertions as Checkpoint 2.

```{r}
# 1. Clean missing IDs and target values
data_cleaned = data |>
  filter(!is.na(id), !is.na(created)) |> # Remove rows without an ID or timestamp
  mutate(comms_num = dplyr::coalesce(comms_num, 0)) # Replace NA comment counts with 0

# 2. Run quality assertions
data_verified = data_cleaned |>
  verify(comms_num >= 0) |> # Engagement counts must be non-negative
  verify(!is.na(id)) |> # Reddit Post IDs must not be NA
  verify(!is.na(created)) |> # Timestamps must exist
  verify(!is.na(title_sarcasm) & title_sarcasm >= 0 & title_sarcasm <= 100) |>
  verify(!is.na(body_sarcasm) & body_sarcasm >= 0 & body_sarcasm <= 100)

# 3. Document dataset dimensions
dim_summary = tibble(
  Stage = c("Post-only Source Dataset", "Cleaned & Verified Dataset"),
  Rows = c(nrow(data_wsb2022_sarcasm), nrow(data_verified)),
  Columns = c(ncol(data_wsb2022_sarcasm), ncol(data_verified))
)

dim_summary |> kable(caption = "Dataset Dimensions Before and After Cleaning")
```

## Build the modeling data set

Here we have added new metrics. We made the metric of high_engagement which is when a post has more than the median number of comments, which is 26. It is used as a helper label and not the target

We also created the outcomes and all candidate features. The predictor sets below use information available at posting time. `score` is excluded because it accrues after the post is created. The distinction of post type we have made based on the URL. 

x 

```{r}
# threshold for "high" engagement (median comment count)
engagement_threshold = median(data_verified$comms_num)
engagement_threshold

# helper: logical -> yes/no factor
# nolint start: object_usage_linter

yn = function(x) factor(if_else(x, "yes", "no"), levels = c("no", "yes"))

# nolint end

# Ticker references and daily prices. The price CSV has two header rows
# (price field, then ticker), followed by a Date row before the observations.
ticker.pattern = "\\$\\^?[A-Za-z]{1,5}(?:[.-][A-Za-z])?\\b"
normalize.ticker = function(x) stringr::str_replace_all(stringr::str_to_upper(x), stringr::fixed("."), "-")

popular.tickers = read_csv("./reference/popular_tickers.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  pull(symbol) %>%
  stringr::str_trim() %>%
  normalize.ticker()

price.header = data.table::fread(
  "./data/SnP_daily_update.csv",
  header = FALSE, nrows = 2, colClasses = "character", showProgress = FALSE
)
close.columns = which(as.character(price.header[1, ]) == "Close")
close.tickers = normalize.ticker(as.character(price.header[2, close.columns, with = FALSE]))

daily.close = data.table::fread(
  "./data/SnP_daily_update.csv",
  skip = 3, header = FALSE, select = c(1L, close.columns),
  col.names = c("post_date", close.tickers), showProgress = FALSE
)

daily.moves = as_tibble(daily.close) %>%
  mutate(post_date = as.Date(post_date)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-post_date, names_to = "title_ticker", values_to = "close") %>%
  group_by(title_ticker) %>%
  arrange(post_date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    previous_close = lag(close),
    ticker_daily_direction = factor(
      case_when(
        is.na(close) | is.na(previous_close) ~ NA_character_,
        close > previous_close ~ "UP",
        close < previous_close ~ "DOWN",
        TRUE ~ "FLAT"
      ),
      levels = c("DOWN", "FLAT", "UP")
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(post_date, title_ticker, ticker_daily_direction)

model.df = data_verified %>%
  mutate(
    # posting time in New York
    ny_dt = lubridate::with_tz(lubridate::as_datetime(created, tz = "UTC"), tzone = "America/New_York"),
    post_date = as.Date(ny_dt, tz = "America/New_York"),
    ny_hour = lubridate::hour(ny_dt),
    market_open = yn(ny_hour >= 9 & ny_hour < 16),
    ny_hour_f = factor(ny_hour, levels = 0:23),
    ny_dow = factor(lubridate::wday(ny_dt, week_start = 1),
      levels = 1:7,
      labels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
    ),
    post_year = factor(lubridate::year(ny_dt)),
    # post type from url
    post_type = factor(
      case_when(
        str_detect(coalesce(url, ""), "(?i)i\\.redd\\.it|\\.(jpe?g|png|gif|webp)(\\?|$)") ~ "image",
        str_detect(coalesce(url, ""), "(?i)v\\.redd\\.it|youtube\\.com|youtu\\.be") ~ "video",
        str_detect(coalesce(url, ""), "(?i)reddit\\.com/gallery") ~ "gallery",
        str_detect(coalesce(url, ""), "(?i)reddit\\.com/r/") ~ "text",
        TRUE ~ "link"
      ),
      levels = c("text", "image", "video", "gallery", "link")
    ),
    # body features
    no_body = yn(no_body),
    log_body_words = log1p(body_work_count),
    # title features
    log_title_chars = log1p(stringr::str_length(title)),
    title_caps_ratio = stringr::str_count(title, "[A-Z]") / pmax(stringr::str_count(title, "[A-Za-z]"), 1),
    title_has_question = yn(stringr::str_detect(title, "\\?")),
    title_has_exclaim = yn(stringr::str_detect(title, "!")),
    title_ticker = normalize.ticker(
      stringr::str_remove(stringr::str_extract(title, ticker.pattern), stringr::fixed("$"))
    ),
    title_has_ticker = yn(!is.na(title_ticker)),
    title_ticker_popular = yn(if_else(is.na(title_ticker), NA, title_ticker %in% popular.tickers)),
    title_has_emoji = yn(stringr::str_detect(title, "\\p{So}")),
    # Independent flags preserve titles that mention both gains and losses.
    title_has_gain = yn(stringr::str_detect(title, "(?i)\\bgains?\\b")),
    title_has_loss = yn(stringr::str_detect(title, "(?i)\\bloss(?:es)?\\b")),
    title_has_kw = yn(
      stringr::str_detect(title, "(?i)\\b(yolo|dd)\\b") |
        title_has_gain == "yes" | title_has_loss == "yes"
    ),
    # outcomes
    log_comms = log1p(comms_num),
    # first factor level is treated as the "event" by yardstick
    high_engagement = factor(if_else(comms_num > engagement_threshold, "high", "low"),
      levels = c("high", "low")
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(daily.moves, by = c("post_date", "title_ticker"), relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
  select(
    post_id = id, comms_num, log_comms, high_engagement,
    title_sarcasm, body_sarcasm,
    log_body_words, no_body, market_open,
    log_title_chars, title_caps_ratio, title_has_question, title_has_exclaim,
    title_has_ticker, title_ticker, title_ticker_popular, ticker_daily_direction,
    title_has_emoji, title_has_kw, title_has_gain, title_has_loss,
    post_type, post_date, ny_dow, ny_hour_f, post_year
  )

head(model.df)
skim(model.df)
```

# class balance
model.df %>%
  count(high_engagement, name = "Posts") %>%
  mutate(Share = 100 * Posts / sum(Posts)) %>%
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "Outcome Class Balance")

# sanity check on the url-based post type rules
model.df %>%
  count(post_type, name = "Posts") %>%
  mutate(Share = 100 * Posts / sum(Posts)) %>%
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "Post Type (derived from url)")

## Train / test split and cross-validation folds

All models below use this same split and these same folds. We used set.seed(42) to make the process repeatable and chose the standard 80/20 split, stratified on high_engagement. This gives about 76k training and 19k test rows, and keeps the high/low balance even though the models predict a continuous response. The 5-fold stratified CV on the training set ensures each model is scored on five different held-out portions of the data, so we can tune and compare models without touching the test set. We note that random vs. time-based splitting is a limitation because posts span 2021 to 2025, so a random split lets models learn from later posts to predict earlier ones and does not test forecasting of future posts.

```{r}
set.seed(42)
wsb.split = initial_split(model.df, prop = 0.8, strata = high_engagement)

wsb.train = training(wsb.split)
wsb.test = testing(wsb.split)

# 5-fold cross validation on the training data
wsb.cv = vfold_cv(wsb.train, v = 5, strata = high_engagement)

c(train = nrow(wsb.train), test = nrow(wsb.test))
```

### Parallel training

Lasso tuning, random forest tuning, and random forest ablation cross-validation run across folds in parallel. Use at most one worker per fold and leave one available CPU core free when possible. On a single-core machine, training runs sequentially. Each forest uses one thread during cross-validation. Workers are released and the previous processing plan is restored after each step, including if training fails.

```{r}
parallel.workers = min(nrow(wsb.cv), parallelly::availableCores(omit = 1))

with.parallel = function(expr) {
  previous.plan = future::plan()
  on.exit(future::plan(previous.plan), add = TRUE)
  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = parallel.workers)
  force(expr)
}

parallel.workers
```

## Predictor sets, recipes, and helper functions
Predictors are grouped into a reduced baseline set, a sarcasm set, and an expanded set. A common recipe normalizes numeric predictors and dummy-codes factors for the linear models (the random forest keeps factors as is), and every model is cross-validated on the same folds and scored with RMSE, MAE and R².


```{r}
# predictor sets
base.vars = c("log_body_words", "no_body", "market_open")
sarc.vars = c("title_sarcasm", "body_sarcasm")
title.vars = c(
  "log_title_chars", "title_caps_ratio", "title_has_question",
  "title_has_exclaim", "title_has_ticker", "title_has_emoji", "title_has_kw"
)
ctx.vars = c("post_type", "ny_dow", "ny_hour_f", "post_year")
# market_open is dropped in the expanded set since ny_hour_f already contains it
exp.vars = c("log_body_words", "no_body", title.vars, ctx.vars)

# model names (used to label results)
m.null = "Null (mean)"
m.blm0 = "Baseline log-linear: no sarcasm"
m.blm1 = "Baseline log-linear: + sarcasm"
m.lm0 = "Expanded log-linear: no sarcasm"
m.lm1 = "Expanded log-linear: + sarcasm"
m.lasso = "Lasso: + sarcasm"
m.rf0 = "Random forest: no sarcasm"
m.rf1 = "Random forest: + sarcasm"
model.levels = c(m.null, m.blm0, m.blm1, m.lm0, m.lm1, m.lasso, m.rf0, m.rf1)
```

```{r}
# nolint start: object_usage_linter.

# recipe builder: linear.prep = TRUE normalizes + dummy codes (linear models),
# FALSE leaves factors alone (random forest). ns.sarcasm adds a spline on title sarcasm.
make.recipe = function(outcome, predictors, ns.sarcasm = FALSE, linear.prep = TRUE) {
  rec = recipe(reformulate(predictors, response = outcome), data = wsb.train)
  if (ns.sarcasm) {
    rec = rec %>% step_ns(title_sarcasm, deg_free = 4)
  }
  if (linear.prep) {
    rec = rec %>%
      step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
      step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
      step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
      step_zv(all_predictors())
  }
  rec
}

# metrics
reg.metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae, rsq)

# cross validation wrapper (same folds for every model)
fit.cv = function(wf, metrics, parallel = FALSE) {
  set.seed(42)
  fit_resamples(
    wf,
    resamples = wsb.cv,
    metrics = metrics,
    control = control_resamples(
      save_pred = TRUE, allow_par = parallel, parallel_over = "resamples"
    )
  )
}

# per-fold regression metrics, optionally restricted to selected tuning parameters
collect.cv.metrics = function(res, name, params = NULL) {
  metrics = collect_metrics(res, summarize = FALSE)
  if (!is.null(params)) {
    metrics = metrics %>% semi_join(params, by = ".config")
  }
  metrics %>%
    select(id, .metric, .estimate) %>%
    mutate(model = name)
}

# regression models: the predicted log count is used as the score for "high"
cv.auc.reg = function(res, name, params = NULL) {
  collect_predictions(res, parameters = params) %>%
    mutate(high_engagement = wsb.train$high_engagement[.row]) %>%
    group_by(id) %>%
    roc_auc(truth = high_engagement, .pred) %>%
    mutate(model = name)
}

# test set predictions in a common format
collect.test = function(fit, name) {
  augment(fit, wsb.test) %>%
    mutate(
      model = name,
      pred_log = .pred
    ) %>%
    select(
      model, post_id, comms_num, log_comms, high_engagement, post_type,
      post_year, ny_dow, title_sarcasm, pred_log
    )
}

# nolint end
```

## Null model (reference)
>the null model or the dummy model predicts the mean. It gives AUC 0.5 and RMSE of about 1.57, the SD of log-comments, and it’s the reference that everything else must beat. 

```{r}
null.mod = null_model() %>%
  set_engine("parsnip") %>%
  set_mode("regression")

null.wf = workflow() %>%
  add_model(null.mod) %>%
  add_recipe(make.recipe("log_comms", base.vars))

null.cv = fit.cv(null.wf, reg.metrics)
null.final = fit(null.wf, wsb.train)

null.cv %>%
  collect_metrics()
```

## Linear regression on log1p(comments): reduced-feature baseline

The baseline is a linear regression of log(1 + comments) on log body word count, whether the post has a body, and whether it was posted during market hours, fit with and without linear title and body sarcasm scores. It sets the floor that later models must beat. 

```{r}
lm.mod = linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm")

blm0.wf = workflow() %>%
  add_model(lm.mod) %>%
  add_recipe(make.recipe("log_comms", base.vars))

blm1.wf = workflow() %>%
  add_model(lm.mod) %>%
  add_recipe(make.recipe("log_comms", c(base.vars, sarc.vars)))

blm1.wf
```

### Cross-validated performance
Under 5-fold CV the baseline is barely better than the null model: RMSE is 1.566 without sarcasm and 1.565 with it (null: 1.571), and R² is under 1%. MAE (about 1.20) is no better than the null’s 1.199.
```{r}
blm0.cv = fit.cv(blm0.wf, reg.metrics)
blm1.cv = fit.cv(blm1.wf, reg.metrics)

bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(blm0.cv) %>% mutate(model = m.blm0),
  collect_metrics(blm1.cv) %>% mutate(model = m.blm1)
) %>%
  select(model, .metric, mean, std_err) %>%
  arrange(.metric, model)
```

### Final fit and test set performance


```{r}
blm0.final = fit(blm0.wf, wsb.train)
blm1.final = fit(blm1.wf, wsb.train)

baseline.test.pred = bind_rows(
  collect.test(blm0.final, m.blm0),
  collect.test(blm1.final, m.blm1)
)

baseline.test.pred %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  reg.metrics(truth = log_comms, estimate = pred_log)
```

```{r}
baseline.test.pred %>%
  filter(model == m.blm1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pred_log, y = log_comms)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05, color = "#1a237e") +
  geom_abline(color = "#d32f2f") +
  labs(x = "Predicted log(1 + comms_num)", y = "Actual log(1 + comms_num)") +
  theme_light()
```

### Coefficients

Coefficients are changes in predicted log comments per 1 SD (or yes vs. no). Posts without a body (−0.50), longer bodies (−0.23 per SD) and market-hours posting (−0.11) are associated with fewer comments, and body sarcasm with slightly more (+0.06 per SD). Title sarcasm is not significant (CI includes 0).

```{r}
blm1.coefs = blm1.final %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  tidy(conf.int = TRUE)

blm1.coefs

blm1.coefs %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = reorder(term, estimate))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Coefficient on log comment count (95% CI)", y = NULL) +
  theme_light()
```

## Baseline model discussion:
The baseline explains under 1% of the variance and is essentially at the null level; adding sarcasm lowers RMSE by less than 0.001. It uses few predictors, treats sarcasm as linear, and omits timing and post-type information, which motivates the expanded models. 


# 3 Advanced model fit

## Log-linear regression on log1p(comments), expanded features

Same expanded feature set with and without sarcasm. With sarcasm, title sarcasm enters as a spline to capture the non-linear trend.

```{r}
lm0.wf = workflow() %>%
  add_model(lm.mod) %>%
  add_recipe(make.recipe("log_comms", exp.vars))

lm1.wf = workflow() %>%
  add_model(lm.mod) %>%
  add_recipe(make.recipe("log_comms", c(exp.vars, sarc.vars), ns.sarcasm = TRUE))

lm0.cv = fit.cv(lm0.wf, reg.metrics)
lm1.cv = fit.cv(lm1.wf, reg.metrics)

lm0.final = fit(lm0.wf, wsb.train)
lm1.final = fit(lm1.wf, wsb.train)

bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(lm0.cv) %>% mutate(model = m.lm0),
  collect_metrics(lm1.cv) %>% mutate(model = m.lm1)
) %>%
  select(model, .metric, mean, std_err) %>%
  arrange(.metric, model)
```

```{r}
# coefficients of the model with sarcasm
lm1.final %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  tidy() %>%
  arrange(p.value) %>%
  head(20)
```

## Lasso regression

Expanded features plus sarcasm. `penalty` is tuned over the shared CV folds.

```{r}
lasso.spec = linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 1) %>%
  set_engine("glmnet")

lasso.wf = workflow() %>%
  add_model(lasso.spec) %>%
  add_recipe(make.recipe("log_comms", c(exp.vars, sarc.vars), ns.sarcasm = TRUE))

lasso.grid = grid_regular(penalty(range = c(-5, -1)), levels = 20)

set.seed(42)
lasso.tune.res = with.parallel(
  tune_grid(
    lasso.wf,
    resamples = wsb.cv,
    grid = lasso.grid,
    metrics = reg.metrics,
    control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE, parallel_over = "resamples")
  )
)
```

```{r}
## Plot the results
lasso.tuning.results = lasso.tune.res %>%
  collect_metrics() %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse" | .metric == "rsq") %>%
  mutate(metric = .metric)

ggplot(lasso.tuning.results, aes(x = penalty, y = mean, group = .metric, color = .metric)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  theme_light() +
  facet_grid(metric ~ ., scales = "free_y")
```

```{r}
lasso.best = select_best(lasso.tune.res, metric = "rmse")
lasso.best

lasso.final.wf = finalize_workflow(lasso.wf, lasso.best)
lasso.final = fit(lasso.final.wf, wsb.train)

# features kept by the lasso
lasso.final %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  tidy() %>%
  filter(estimate != 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate)))
```

## Random forest

Expanded features plus sarcasm. `mtry` and `min_n` are tuned over the shared CV folds (this step can take several minutes).

```{r}
rf.trees = 300

# Embed fixed settings in the specification so workers do not need global variables.
rf.spec = rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = !!rf.trees) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", num.threads = 1, respect.unordered.factors = "order") %>%
  set_mode("regression")

rf1.rec = make.recipe("log_comms", c(exp.vars, sarc.vars), linear.prep = FALSE)
rf0.rec = make.recipe("log_comms", exp.vars, linear.prep = FALSE)

rf.wf = workflow() %>%
  add_model(rf.spec) %>%
  add_recipe(rf1.rec)

rf.grid = grid_regular(mtry(range = c(3L, 12L)), min_n(range = c(10L, 100L)), levels = 3)

set.seed(42)
rf.tune.res = with.parallel(
  tune_grid(
    rf.wf,
    resamples = wsb.cv,
    grid = rf.grid,
    metrics = reg.metrics,
    control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE, parallel_over = "resamples")
  )
)
```

```{r}
## Plot the results
rf.tuning.results = rf.tune.res %>%
  collect_metrics() %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse")

ggplot(rf.tuning.results, aes(x = mtry, y = mean, group = factor(min_n), color = factor(min_n))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(color = "min_n", y = "CV RMSE (log scale)") +
  theme_light()
```

```{r}
rf.best = select_best(rf.tune.res, metric = "rmse")
rf.best

# final model WITH sarcasm: permutation importance for the variable importance plot
rf.final.spec = rand_forest(mtry = rf.best$mtry, min_n = rf.best$min_n, trees = rf.trees) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "permutation", respect.unordered.factors = "order") %>%
  set_mode("regression")

rf1.final.wf = workflow() %>%
  add_model(rf.final.spec) %>%
  add_recipe(rf1.rec)

set.seed(42)
rf1.final = fit(rf1.final.wf, wsb.train)
```

### Random forest without sarcasm (ablation)

Same tuned hyperparameters and same folds, sarcasm features removed.

```{r}
rf.cv.spec = rand_forest(mtry = !!rf.best$mtry, min_n = !!rf.best$min_n, trees = !!rf.trees) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", num.threads = 1, respect.unordered.factors = "order") %>%
  set_mode("regression")

rf0.wf = workflow() %>%
  add_model(rf.cv.spec) %>%
  add_recipe(rf0.rec)

rf0.cv = with.parallel(fit.cv(rf0.wf, reg.metrics, parallel = TRUE))

set.seed(42)
rf0.final = fit(rf0.wf, wsb.train)
```

### Variable importance

```{r}
rf1.importance = rf1.final %>%
  extract_fit_engine() %>%
  .$variable.importance %>%
  enframe(name = "feature", value = "importance")

ggplot(rf1.importance, aes(x = importance, y = reorder(feature, importance))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2b5c8f") +
  labs(x = "Permutation importance", y = NULL) +
  theme_light()
```

# 4 Model evaluation

## Collect results for all models

```{r}
# per-fold regression metrics (same folds and response for every model)
cv.reg.fold = bind_rows(
  collect.cv.metrics(null.cv, m.null),
  collect.cv.metrics(blm0.cv, m.blm0),
  collect.cv.metrics(blm1.cv, m.blm1),
  collect.cv.metrics(lm0.cv, m.lm0),
  collect.cv.metrics(lm1.cv, m.lm1),
  collect.cv.metrics(lasso.tune.res, m.lasso, params = lasso.best),
  collect.cv.metrics(rf0.cv, m.rf0),
  collect.cv.metrics(rf.tune.res, m.rf1, params = rf.best)
)

cv.reg = cv.reg.fold %>%
  group_by(model, .metric) %>%
  summarise(cv_mean = mean(.estimate), cv_sd = sd(.estimate), .groups = "drop")

# test set predictions (same held-out test set for every model)
test.pred.all = bind_rows(
  collect.test(null.final, m.null),
  baseline.test.pred,
  collect.test(lm0.final, m.lm0),
  collect.test(lm1.final, m.lm1),
  collect.test(lasso.final, m.lasso),
  collect.test(rf0.final, m.rf0),
  collect.test(rf1.final, m.rf1)
)

test.reg = test.pred.all %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  reg.metrics(truth = log_comms, estimate = pred_log) %>%
  select(model, .metric, test = .estimate)
```

## Primary comparison: regression metrics (log scale)

All models are evaluated against the same `log_comms` response. Lower RMSE and MAE indicate more accurate log-count predictions. The reduced and expanded linear models distinguish the benefit of the expanded specification from the additional effects of regularization or a random forest.

```{r}
cv.reg %>%
  select(-cv_sd) %>%
  left_join(test.reg, by = c("model", ".metric")) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = model.levels)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = .metric, values_from = c(cv_mean, test)) %>%
  arrange(model) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Regression Metrics on log1p(comms_num): All Models")
```

```{r}
rmse.summary = cv.reg %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse") %>%
  left_join(test.reg, by = c("model", ".metric")) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = model.levels))

ggplot(rmse.summary, aes(y = fct_rev(model))) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(x = cv_mean, xmin = cv_mean - cv_sd, xmax = cv_mean + cv_sd)) +
  geom_point(aes(x = test), shape = 4, size = 3, color = "#d32f2f") +
  labs(
    x = "RMSE on log(1 + comms_num) (lower is better)", y = NULL,
    caption = "Black = CV mean +/- 1 SD, red X = test set"
  ) +
  theme_light()
```

## Does sarcasm help? (paired fold differences in RMSE)

```{r}
cv.rmse.wide = cv.reg.fold %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse") %>%
  select(id, model, .estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = .estimate)

ablation = cv.rmse.wide %>%
  transmute(
    id,
    `Baseline log-linear` = .data[[m.blm1]] - .data[[m.blm0]],
    `Expanded log-linear` = .data[[m.lm1]] - .data[[m.lm0]],
    `Random forest` = .data[[m.rf1]] - .data[[m.rf0]]
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(-id, names_to = "model.family", values_to = "delta_rmse")

ablation %>%
  group_by(model.family) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_delta = mean(delta_rmse), sd_delta = sd(delta_rmse),
    min_delta = min(delta_rmse), max_delta = max(delta_rmse)
  ) %>%
  kable(
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Change in CV RMSE from adding sarcasm features (negative = improvement)"
  )

ggplot(ablation, aes(x = model.family, y = delta_rmse)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "RMSE with sarcasm minus RMSE without (negative = improvement)") +
  theme_light()
```

## Secondary comparison: AUC for high vs. low engagement

Predicted log counts are used only as ranking scores here. This analysis measures discrimination of the binary engagement label and supplements the primary regression comparison.

```{r}
cv.auc = bind_rows(
  cv.auc.reg(null.cv, m.null),
  cv.auc.reg(blm0.cv, m.blm0),
  cv.auc.reg(blm1.cv, m.blm1),
  cv.auc.reg(lm0.cv, m.lm0),
  cv.auc.reg(lm1.cv, m.lm1),
  cv.auc.reg(lasso.tune.res, m.lasso, params = lasso.best),
  cv.auc.reg(rf0.cv, m.rf0),
  cv.auc.reg(rf.tune.res, m.rf1, params = rf.best)
)

test.auc = test.pred.all %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  roc_auc(truth = high_engagement, pred_log) %>%
  select(model, test_auc = .estimate)

auc.summary = cv.auc %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    cv_auc_mean = mean(.estimate), cv_auc_sd = sd(.estimate), .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(test.auc, by = "model") %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = model.levels)) %>%
  arrange(model)

auc.summary %>%
  kable(
    digits = 3, col.names = c("Model", "CV AUC (mean)", "CV AUC (SD)", "Test AUC"),
    caption = "Secondary ROC AUC for High vs. Low Engagement"
  )
```

## ROC curves on the test set

```{r}
test.pred.all %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = model.levels)) %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  roc_curve(truth = high_engagement, pred_log) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = 1 - specificity, y = sensitivity, color = model)) +
  geom_path() +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +

```

## Where do the models fail?

```{r}
# predicted vs. actual for the random forest (test set, log scale)
test.pred.all %>%
  filter(model == m.rf1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pred_log, y = log_comms)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05, color = "#1a237e") +
  geom_abline(color = "#d32f2f") +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", color = "#ff6f00") +
  labs(x = "Predicted log(1 + comms_num)", y = "Actual log(1 + comms_num)") +
  theme_light()
```

```{r}
# residuals by post type and by year: systematic errors
resid.df = test.pred.all %>%
  filter(model %in% c(m.blm1, m.lm1, m.rf1)) %>%
  mutate(resid = log_comms - pred_log)

p_type = ggplot(resid.df, aes(x = post_type, y = resid, fill = model)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_light()

p_year = ggplot(resid.df, aes(x = post_year, y = resid, fill = model)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_light()

p_type / p_year
```

```{r}
# RMSE by subgroup (test set): reduced baseline vs. expanded linear vs. random forest
subgroup.rmse = bind_rows(
  test.pred.all %>%
    filter(model %in% c(m.blm1, m.lm1, m.rf1)) %>%
    group_by(model, group = "post_type", level = as.character(post_type)) %>%
    rmse(truth = log_comms, estimate = pred_log),
  test.pred.all %>%
    filter(model %in% c(m.blm1, m.lm1, m.rf1)) %>%
    group_by(model, group = "post_year", level = as.character(post_year)) %>%
    rmse(truth = log_comms, estimate = pred_log)
)

ggplot(subgroup.rmse, aes(x = level, y = .estimate, color = model, group = model)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(. ~ group, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Test RMSE on log(1 + comms_num)") +
  theme_light()
```
